# Independent audit: multi-input barycentric coupling and seven-fiber credit

Source: `candidate 4bb4c167681e8955`, Sections 1–5.

Result: **PASS**. This is an independent mathematical read; the coupling proof uses exact identities rather than a finite-dimensional numerical check.

The conditional slice volumes are positive and continuous on the interiors of the actual projected bodies. The truncated-volume numerator in each conditional CDF is concave after its appropriate dimensional root, on its open positive domain. This justifies joint continuity without assuming derivatives in earlier coordinates. The inverse maps have positive continuous own-coordinate derivatives; their telescoping product is the body volume.

The weighted sum map stays triangular and has continuous endpoint functions in its cube prefix, hence in the image prefix through the successive inverse. Its injectivity and recursive open image follow. Repeated last-coordinate substitution proves the density formula without cross derivatives or a multidimensional area theorem. With q_j=lambda_j v_j^(1/d)/sum lambda_h v_h^(1/d), weighted AM–GM gives the printed pointwise Jacobian-product bound exactly. The support and centroid statements follow for the same fixed coupling; no normal-dependent law is substituted. The boundary-null argument and d=1 case are valid.

The source-budget accounting uses full t_E per endpoint, not barycentric lambda_Ez t_E. Expanding eta, Delta, and the unused fractions in equation (10) cancels each allocated contribution exactly. The pointwise implication uses closed affine margins and remains true with whole-fiber boundary mass. The pair-intersection bound (11) is correctly oriented for every captured source count k. The d=0 convention is separated from the determinant proof.

For the ordered reflected-pair certificate, identical endpoint bodies are contained in the anchor by actual midpoint inclusion. At Y=g_1, normals with u dot w>=0 put each paired threshold at or below its own paired-centroid threshold; normals with u dot w<=0 put the own cap through or below g_0. Thus the two lower bounds in (14) cover all continuous normals. The pure-integer bound retains the whole anchor fiber and at least one member of every pair, and it dominates the displayed Gamma bound. A containing cap can be moved to Y in the correct direction without increasing captured mass.

The seven-fiber arithmetic checks directly: sum pair masses=7/8, total=11/4, the two bracket terms are17/8 and37/16, and the chosen point obtains17/18, exceeding11/18 by1/3. This retains the actual centroid ordering, so it does not contradict the earlier scalar-envelope obstruction. Binary padding keeps the original denominator and same raw OC target.

No correction requested. The source properly identifies general anchor selection as missing rather than asserting it from the coupling or the calibration.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
